segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
[son] of Antiochus the Great,
who had been a hostage in Rome for eleven years.
And as soon as he became king, he went against Ptolemy to Egypt.
And when he was turned back by the Romans,
he returned to Judea.
And when he came to Jerusalem,
he plundered the temple of God,
and set up in it the statue of Zeus.
And he seized Eleazar the priest to offer sacrifice;
and when he would not consent,
he died after tortures.
And after him they brought Shmuni, the wife of Shalom, with her seven sons before Antiochus.
And to the first they cut out his tongue and the ends of all his limbs,
and threw him into a frying pan.
And of the second, they stripped off the skin of his head.
And of the third, likewise, they cut out his tongue.
And thus to the other four,
and finally to their mother they did [the same].
And while they were crowned [with martyrdom] in Jerusalem,
afterwards their bodies were brought to Antioch.
[Dynasty/Rule] Thirty-five.
In the sixteenth year of his own reign, Antiochus Epiphanes died in the land of the Persians of a bitter disease, a plague from God.
And Antiochus Eupator reigned for two years.
And this one also multiplied evils upon the Jews.
In his time Mattathias, the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest from the sons of Jonadab, was living in Modin.
And he had five sons:
John Gaddi,
and Simeon Tharsi,
and Judas Maccabaeus,
and Eleazar Avaran,
and Jonathan Apphus.
These, when they saw a certain Jew sacrificing,
were filled with zeal and killed him, and also the commissioner who was compelling them to sacrifice;
and they tore down the altar.
And the brothers fled with other zealots of the Law to the mountain.
And when Antiochus Eupator heard, he sent an army of one hundred thousand to Jerusalem.
And while they were fighting,
Eleazar Avaran saw a large elephant,
and thought that the king was sitting upon it.
And he went under it,
and pierced its belly with a sword.
The elephant, however, collapsed and fell upon him,
and he died.
And when the battle ceased and they were gathering the corpses for burial,
they found under the garments of each one of them [some] of the gold of the idols.
Judas, however, sent three thousand [drachmas] of silver to the priests in Jerusalem,
that they should offer a sacrifice on behalf of those who had died,
and make atonement for them,
because
